\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{حکومت} (hokumat)}{حکومت (hokumat)}]{\fa{حکومت} (hokumat) — a government, rule}

\label{lesson:FA-C409-hokumat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for corruption, then the Persian for a charge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{حکومت}}
\textbf{\fa{حکومت}} (\emph{hokumat}) — \textquotedblleft{}a government, rule\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{زمان} \fa{حکومت} \fa{در} \fa{دست} \fa{یک} \fa{پادشاه} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dar ân zamân hokumat dar dast-e yek pâdeshâh bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At that time power was in the hands of a king.
\end{quote}

\emph{Hokumat kardan} — to rule. \emph{Dowlat} is the government of the day.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{حکومت}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ḥukūma} \textquotedblleft{}government\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from the same Arabic family as \emph{ḥukm} \textquotedblleft{}ruling\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hokumat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hokumat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for corruption, then the Persian for a charge, then say \emph{hokumat} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سیاست} (siyâsat)}{سیاست (siyâsat)}]{\fa{سیاست} (siyâsat) — politics; a policy}

\label{lesson:FA-C409-siyasat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a charge, then the Persian for a government.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سیاست}}
\textbf{\fa{سیاست}} (\emph{siyâsat}) — \textquotedblleft{}politics; a policy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{به} \fa{سیاست} \fa{علاقه} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedaram be siyâsat 'alâqe dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father is interested in politics.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{siyâsathâ}, policies. \emph{Siyâsatmadâr} — a politician.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{سیاست}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{siyāsa} \textquotedblleft{}policy, politics\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{انتخابات} (entekhâbât)}{انتخابات (entekhâbât)}]{\fa{انتخابات} (entekhâbât) — an election, elections}

\label{lesson:FA-C409-entekhabat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a government, then the Persian for politics.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{انتخابات}}
\textbf{\fa{انتخابات}} (\emph{entekhâbât}) — \textquotedblleft{}an election, elections\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{انتخابات} \fa{سال} \fa{آینده} \fa{برگزار} \fa{میشود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{entekhâbât sâl-e âyande bargozâr mishavad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The election will be held next year.
\end{quote}

The Arabic-style plural of \emph{entekhâb} \textquotedblleft{}choice\textquotedblright{}, the usual word for an election.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{انتخابات}} is the Arabic-style plural of \emph{entekhâb} \textquotedblleft{}choice\textquotedblright{}, from Arabic \emph{intikhāb} \textquotedblleft{}choosing\textquotedblright{}: an election is many choices.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رای} \fa{دادن} (ra'y dâdan)}{رای دادن (ra'y dâdan)}]{\fa{رای} \fa{دادن} (ra'y dâdan) — to vote}

\label{lesson:FA-C409-ray-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for politics, then the Persian for an election.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رای} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{رای} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{ra'y dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to vote\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ما} \fa{فردا} \fa{رای} \fa{میدهیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâ fardâ ra'y midahim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We vote tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ra'y} \textquotedblleft{}opinion; vote\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dâdan} (stem \emph{deh-}). \emph{Be kasi ra'y dâdan} — to vote for someone. Many writers put a hamza on the alef of \emph{ra'y}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{رای}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ra'y} \textquotedblleft{}opinion, view\textquotedblright{}; with \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB traces it to PIE \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-}), you give your opinion at the ballot box.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ra'y dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ra'y dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for politics, then the Persian for an election, then say \emph{ra'y dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مجلس} (majles)}{مجلس (majles)}]{\fa{مجلس} (majles) — parliament; a gathering}

\label{lesson:FA-C409-majles}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an election, then the Persian for to vote.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مجلس}}
\textbf{\fa{مجلس}} (\emph{majles}) — \textquotedblleft{}parliament; a gathering\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نماینده} \fa{ما} \fa{در} \fa{مجلس} \fa{سخنرانی} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{namâyande-ye mâ dar majles sokhanrâni kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our representative gave a speech in parliament.
\end{quote}

Iran's parliament is the \emph{majles}. Also a formal gathering.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مجلس}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{majlis} \textquotedblleft{}place of sitting, session\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): a parliament is where its members sit.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
